title: Farouk's Hybrid Athlete Program
author: farouk S.
desc:
Adapted from Bryan Boorstein's Hybrid Athlete Program, rebuilt for bodyweight training and organized around combat sport.

---

This is a hybrid program for the bodyweight athlete who also fights. It takes the framework of Bryan Boorstein's Hybrid Athlete Program (his blend of strength, hypertrophy, and structured cardio) and adapts it in two ways.

The result trains everything at once; muscle, strength, and endurance across every intensity, without any single quality crowding out the others, and without leaving you too beat-up to roll.

The Block

Run as an 11-week cycle, kept from the original structure:

5 weeks of progressive building

1 week deload to reset and let the work catch up to you

5 weeks of building again

Run it back as many times as you want; each cycle you come back stronger, more muscular, and harder to gas.

The Training Week

Three calisthenics strength days

Two upper-body sessions (chest, back, shoulders), placed on your Sambo days

One lower-body and arms session, built around a loaded squat, on a clean day with no fighting

Two combat days

Sambo plus live sparring, stacked onto the two upper-lifting days

A full spectrum of conditioning

Two easy Zone 2 sessions to build and hold the aerobic base

One threshold session; controlled, sustainable hard effort

One long run for pure aerobic volume

VO2-max intervals on weeks you don't spar, since hard sparring already trains the same top-end engine

Short speed strides tagged onto an easy day to keep the fast-twitch fibers awake

An optional core session

A Sample Week

Day 1 — Upper body (chest/back/delts) + Sambo & sparring (VO2 intervals only on weeks you don't spar)

Day 2 — Easy Zone 2 cardio + speed strides

Day 3 — Upper body (chest/back/delts), lighter volume + Sambo & sparring

Day 4 — Easy Zone 2 cardio + core

Day 5 — Lower body (loaded squat + hinge) & arms

Day 6 — Threshold intervals

Day 7 — Long run (or rest and mobility)

The Point

The goal isn't to be good at one thing. It's to be a complete athlete — strong, muscular, hard to tire, and sharp on the mat — with a week you can actually recover from and repeat.

Warm-Up

5–10 minutes before every session to warm up and prep the joints you'll load.

Every session: light cardio until you break a sweat, then dynamic mobility; leg swings, hip circles, T-spine rotations, bodyweight squats. Save static stretching for after!

Upper + Sambo days (1 & 3):

Wrists (circles + palms-down/palms-up floor stretches)

Shoulders (rolls, arm circles, band pull-aparts and pass-throughs)

Neck (slow rotations + light bridging)

A few easy band presses and rows before loading.

Squat day (5): extra hips and ankles — deep squats, ankle rocks, lunges.

Speed day (2): after the easy run, a couple of build-up accelerations before your strides.

Threshold & long run (6 & 7): start the first few minutes easy.
